peer protocol behavior: BIP152 compact block negotiation and reconstruction, BIP37 filters, the mempool message and blocks-only mode, headers announcement, locators, fingerprinting protections, extversion handshake (enabled, disabled, no misbehavior score), address relay, connection/ban/permission handling, message framing (magic, checksum, command, oversized payload), transaction download scheduling and inv batching, request of invalid blocks; each verifies how a peer is served or disconnected, none a validity rule (p2p_tx_download and p2p_leak_tx concern when transactions are requested and announced)

Knuth intentionally applies its own local policy, initially with consensus-equivalent parameters. BCHN standardness is an independent reference API, not a condition for Knuth admission. The earlier RED below assumed BCHN enforcement and is retained as historical comparison evidence.
entries.omitted: the wallet half (sending to the address, abandoning the transaction)
entries.relayRoute: the same transactions through blockchain::block_chain::organize(transaction) (mempool insert + subscribe_transaction announcement): organize answers success, inserts into the mempool and announces them where BCHN refuses (RED, evidence round9/standardness_organize, 20 sections, 80 failed checks), and gives the same codes as transaction_validate for the transactions both refuse (controls in src/node/test/bchn_standardness_organize.cpp)
entries.historicalReason: a transaction paying to a P2SH32 address is refused as scriptpubkey before the P2SH32 activation and accepted after it: before Upgrade 9 (phase by settings) Knuth validates it as success; after it, accepted (control)
entries.policyProfile: BCHN reference compared with Knuth local admission
entries.fidelity: The reference API and representative admission cases are checked; this does not port every original functional peer/RPC path.

ReadCompactSize refuses a value above MAX_SIZE (0x02000000). Executed at the endpoints that read a size: the transaction input count, the block transaction count and a script length, for 0x02000001, 0x10000000 and 0x7fffffff, with data too short for the announced size: every endpoint refuses (as BCHN, with another reason). At function level Knuth read_size_little_endian has no such bound; the endpoints bound the value at 2,000,000,000 (static_absolute_max_block_size) and by the data that follows

upstream.subcase: BIP113 locktime by median time past

entries.reason: BIP113: a time-based locktime above the median time past of the previous block and below the block time, with a non-final sequence, is accepted in a block; BCHN refuses it (bad-txns-nonfinal). Executed with the locktime below the MTP as control

upstream.subcase: oversized output is not added to the UTXO set

entries.reason: an output with a scriptPubKey over 10000 bytes (script::is_unspendable) is not added to the UTXO set by BCHN; Knuth utxo_builder prunes OP_RETURN only, so it is stored after its block connects (spending it is still refused, at script evaluation). State difference, same rejection outcome

upstream.subcase: removeRecursive of a parent that is not pooled

entries.reason: removeRecursive of a transaction that is not itself in the pool, with its children in the pool (BCHN reorg path when a parent cannot be re-admitted): Knuth has no operation that removes a transaction and its in-pool descendants by id; remove_for_block leaves the children of a confirmed transaction in place

upstream.subcase: the node continues after the refusal

entries.reason: after the block with the duplicate coinbase is refused, BCHN goes on (an ordinary invalid block); Knuth leaves a transition record in progress (read_transition_record: recovery_required) and the UTXO gate answers recovery_required to every read (utxo_count, get_utxo), so the original outputs cannot be read and a valid sibling branch cannot be connected until the database is rebuilt
